key_insight: A structure-only predictor with conformal risk control selects configurations for DFT while controlling the MLIP error retained on unselected configurations.
engineering_relevance: Risk-controlled DFT routing can reduce expensive labeling in automated materials discovery without requiring access to MLIP internals.
method: Convert atomic numbers and Cartesian coordinates into fixed geometric descriptors.
Predict MLIP–DFT disagreement in energy, average force, and maximum force.
Calibrate a DFT-selection threshold using conformal risk control and a user-chosen error fraction α.
evidence_signal: Across eight dataset–MLIP pairs under an identical guarantee, the predictor routed 7% and 14% fewer configurations to DFT than committee baselines at α = 0.3.
watch_item: The guarantee controls aggregate retained error, not every configuration’s accuracy; gains also narrow when DFT labeling settings match MLIP training settings.
paper_title: Risk-Controlled DFT Selection for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
